lines.text: אהו 18 אהל
row, and imitating the sound or cry, ah!
alas! comp. Arab. آهْ, أَوَّاهِ, whence the
verbs أَهَّ and آهَ to grieve, lament, like
Germ. ach, ächzen. Mostly in the con-
nection אֲהָהּ אֲדֹנָי יְהוִה ah! Lord God,
Josh. 7, 7. Judg. 6, 22; or אֲהָהּ אֲדֹנָי 2 K.
6, 5. 15. Alone, 2 K. 3, 10; c. dat. Joel
אֵהוּד (union, r. אָחַד) Ehud, pr. n. m.
a) A judge of Israel, Judg. 3, 15 sq. 4, 1.
Sept. Ἀώδ. b) 1 Chr. 7, 10.
אַהֲוָא Ahava, pr. n. of a river between
Babylon and Jerusalem, Ezra 8, 21. 31.
The same is probably meant in v. 15,
where we may render: the river that
runneth to the Ahava. It is hardly
doubtful, that the word signifies pr. wa-
ter, aqua; comp. Sanscr. ap, Pers. ab,
Goth. ahva, Lat. aqua. It is hard to
say what river is meant; possibly the
Euphrates, which was called κατ᾽ ἐξοχήν
the river; comp. הַנָּהָר.
אֱהִי Hos. 13, 10, i. q. אַיֵּה, אֵי, where?
Elsewhere אֱהִי is always 1 pers. fut.
apoc. from r. הָיָה to be; and not improb.
it is here an error of transcription arising
out of v. 7. 14, instead of אַיֵּה. The
words are אֱהִי מַלְכְּךָ אֵפוֹא where then is
thy king? the two words אֱהִי אֵפוֹא be-
ing closely joined, as elsewhere אֵי אֵפוֹא.
—Ewald regards this word (Gr. § 444) as
compounded from אֱ (i. q. הֲ) and הִי i. e.
hic, here; comp. Ethiop. ህየ ibi, ዝየ
hic, huc. So too Hupfeld.
* אָהַל perh. i. q. הָלַל, هَلَّ 1. to shine,
to glitter, from the mutual relation of
verbs פ״א and ע״ע; see Hiph.—Hence
אֹהֶל tent, from the shining, glittering
appearance.
2. Denom. from אֹהֶל tent, to tent, to
move one’s tent, in the manner of no-
mades, now pitching their tents in one
place and then removing to another.
Gen. 13, 12. 18 וַיֶּאֱהַל אַבְרָם, Sept. ἀπο-
σκηνώσας Ἀβράμ, Vulg. movens taberna-
culum suum.
Piel, fut. יְאַהֵל contr. יַהֵל, i. q. Kal no.
2, to pitch one’s tent, in the nomadic man-
ner, Is. 13, 20. Comp. מַלֵּף for מְאַלֵּף.
Hiph. i. q. Kal no. 1, to shine, pr. to
give light. Job 25, 5 הֵן עַד־יָרֵחַ וְלֹא־
יַאֲהִיל lo! even the moon, it shineth not,
i. e. is not bright, pure, in the sight of
God. Jerome: ecce! luna etiam non
splendet. Sept. οὐκ ἐπιφαύσκει.
The deriv. follow.
אֹהֶל c. suff. אָהֳלִי, אָהֳלְךָ (ŏhŏlka),
with He parag. אֹהֱלָה; Plur. אֹהָלִים
Syriasm for אֳהָלִים Lehrg. p. 152, 572;
with pref. בָּאֳהָלִים Judg. 8, 11. Jer. 35, 7.
10; constr. אָהֳלֵי, c. suff. אֹהָלָיו, אֹהָלֶיךָ,
אָהֳלֵיכֶם.
1. a tent, tabernacle, Gen. 9, 27. al.
אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד tabernacle of the congregation
or of assembly, comm. tabernacle of the
covenant, i. e. the movable and portable
sanctuary of the Israelites in the desert,
described Ex. c. 26, comp. c. 36; also
called simply הָאֹהֶל 1. K. 1, 39. As to
the distinction in the tabernacle, between
אֹהֶל and מִשְׁכָּן, the former (אֹהֶל) denoted
the exterior covering, consisting of
twelve curtains of goats' hair, which was
placed over the proper dwelling (מִשְׁכָּן)
i. e. the twelve interior curtains or hang-
ings which lay upon the frame-work;
2. a dwelling, habitation, house, Is.
16, 5 אֹהֶל דָּוִד the habitation of David.
Ps. 132, 3 אִם אָבֹא בְּאֹהֶל בֵּיתִי I will not
enter the dwelling of my house.
3. Spec. the temple, Ez. 41, 1.
4. Ohel, pr. n. of a son of Zerubbabel,
אָהֳלָה Oholah, Aholah, pr. n. of a
harlot, used by Ezekiel as the symbol
of Samaria, Ez. 23, 4 sq. Put for אָהֳלָהּ
(Mappik) i. e. she has her tent, her own
tabernacle, temple.
אֲהָלוֹת see in אֲהָלִים.
אָהֳלִיאָב (tent of his father) Aholiab,
pr. n. of an artificer, Ex. 31, 6. 35, 34.
אָהֳלִיבָה Oholibah, Aholibah, pr. n. of
a harlot, used by Ezekiel as the symbol
of the idolatrous kingdom of Judah, Ez.
23, 4 sq. lit. my tabernacle is in her, בָה
for בָּהּ. Comp. אָהֳלָה.
אָהֳלִיבָמָה (tent of the height) Aholi-
bamah, pr. n. of a wife of Esau, Gen. 36,
2. 14; also of an Edomitish tribe, v. 14.
אֲהָלִים Num. 24, 6. Prov. 7, 17, and
אֲהָלוֹת Ps. 45, 9. Cant. 4, 14, Plur. a spe-

line_status.note: The decisive letter is the last glyph of the left-hand word: it is a narrow vertical stroke with only a small head, about a third the width of the preceding he, i.e. a vav; a resh in this typeface would have a broad flat head nearly as wide as the he. Read as אהו, matching Reading B.
First Arabic word carries a small circle (sukun) over the ha, not tanwin; second word shows a tall alif before the final ha with a kasra printed beneath it, matching أَوَّاهِ rather than A's أَوَّهْ.
The he in the parenthesis carries a hataf patah (short horizontal stroke plus two dots beneath), not a qamats; this is the interrogative הֲ, paralleling the hataf segol under the preceding alef.
Under the ה of אהלך the print shows ḥaṭeph qamats (ֳ), matching the first word אָהֳלִי and the transliteration ŏhŏlka; Reading A's plain qamats is wrong.

Under the lamed of אֹהָלָיו the print shows a qamets (T-shaped), not a patah — matching the normal 3 m. sg. suffix form; the typographic space before the semicolon ("10 ;") is also printed, as in "572 ;" on the line above.

Under the aleph in both Hebrew words the printed compound sheva has a flat dash (hataf patah ֲ), not the T-shaped qamets of hataf qamets (contrast the clear hataf qamets under the he of אָהֳלִיאָב on the next line). Reading A's ֳ is wrong; B's vowels are right. The period follows the last word directly (B's extra space is just type spacing).
The final he on line 1 has no mappiq dot; the next line's "for בָּהּ" shows the pointed form with mappiq and dagesh as the contrast, so line 1 is the unpointed בָה.
